name: Duration-hazard phase reversal
note: Bull and bear phases are dated causally with a Pagan-Sossounov style rule on closes: bar t is a peak if it is the maximum of C_{t-w..t+w} and a trough if it is the minimum, judged only once bar t+w exists, with alternation enforced, a minimum phase length of dh_min bars, a minimum amplitude of dh_amp between consecutive turning points, and the usual replacement rule (a deeper trough found while still looking for a peak simply moves the trough). The empirical distribution of COMPLETED phase durations is kept separately for bull and bear phases and grows as the backtest runs, so the hazard is always estimated from what had already happened. Long when the current phase is a bear, its age exceeds the dh_in-th percentile of completed bear durations, and price has just crossed dh_conf*ATR above the phase's running minimum within the last dh_recent bars; short is the mirror. Exit when a turning point of the opposite type is dated, or when the position's own age exceeds the dh_out-th percentile of the other phase type's durations; the 2.5*ATR trailing stop is left to the shared harness. Deviation from the idea as written: the source rescaled a monthly rule to daily (21-bar window, 8% amplitude) and this study runs 5-minute bars, so the amplitude is rescaled again - 8% between consecutive turning points would date two or three phases in the whole sample and the percentile would be meaningless. dh_minph refuses to trade at all until that many completed phases of the relevant type exist, so the first stretch of every backtest is spent estimating the hazard rather than betting on it. The amplitude grid was chosen by measurement, not taste: at 2% between consecutive turning points a 45-day 5-minute sample of SPY or XLU dates too few completed phases to form a percentile and the family never trades at all, so the swept range is 0.25% to 1%; at the 0.5% default the probe symbols date 15 to 49 completed phases of each type, with median phase lengths of 40 to 93 bars.
source: Pagan & Sossounov (2003), 'A Simple Framework for Analysing Bull and Bear Markets', Journal of Applied Econometrics 18(1):23-46 - the censoring rules for turning-point dating. Lunde & Timmermann (2004), 'Duration Dependence in Stock Prices: An Analysis of Bull and Bear Markets', JBES 22(3) - positive duration dependence in phase termination. Bulla & Bulla (2006), 'Stylized facts of financial time series and hidden semi-Markov models', CSDA 51.
code:
def family_init(ctx):
    bars = ctx.bars
    n = len(bars)
    w = max(3, int(ctx.p.dh_w))
    mp = max(2, int(ctx.p.dh_min))
    amp = max(0.0005, float(ctx.p.dh_amp))
    p_in = min(0.95, max(0.05, float(ctx.p.dh_in) / 100.0))
    p_out = min(0.99, max(0.10, float(ctx.p.dh_out) / 100.0))
    conf = max(0.1, float(ctx.p.dh_conf))
    rec = max(1, int(ctx.p.dh_recent))
    minph = max(2, int(ctx.p.dh_minph))
    an = max(2, int(ctx.p.dh_atr))

    c = [float(b["c"]) for b in bars]
    h = [float(b["h"]) for b in bars]
    l = [float(b["l"]) for b in bars]

    # plain SMA-of-true-range ATR, computed here so the dating loop can use it
    tr = [0.0] * n
    for i in range(n):
        if i == 0:
            tr[i] = h[i] - l[i]
        else:
            tr[i] = max(h[i] - l[i], abs(h[i] - c[i - 1]), abs(l[i] - c[i - 1]))
    atr = [None] * n
    run = 0.0
    for i in range(n):
        run += tr[i]
        if i >= an:
            run -= tr[i - an]
        if i >= an - 1:
            atr[i] = run / an

    # ---- causal Bry-Boschan / Pagan-Sossounov turning-point dating -----
    # bar t is judged only once bar t+w exists, so nothing is dated with
    # information the strategy did not have.
    last_i = None
    last_p = None
    last_ty = None            # 'P' after a peak (we are in a bear phase)
    d_bull = []               # completed trough->peak durations
    d_bear = []               # completed peak->trough durations
    ph_ty = [None] * n
    ph_age = [0] * n
    ph_min = [None] * n
    ph_max = [None] * n
    n_p = [0] * n
    n_t = [0] * n
    thr_in = [None] * n
    thr_out = [None] * n
    cnt_p = 0
    cnt_t = 0
    cmin = None
    cmax = None

    for i in range(n):
        t = i - w
        if t >= w:
            x = c[t]
            ismax = True
            ismin = True
            for k in range(t - w, t + w + 1):
                if c[k] > x:
                    ismax = False
                if c[k] < x:
                    ismin = False
                if not ismax and not ismin:
                    break
            changed = False
            if last_ty is None:
                if ismax:
                    last_ty, last_i, last_p, changed = "P", t, x, True
                elif ismin:
                    last_ty, last_i, last_p, changed = "T", t, x, True
            elif last_ty == "T":
                if ismin and x < last_p:
                    last_i, last_p, changed = t, x, True
                elif ismax and (t - last_i) >= mp and last_p > 0 and \
                        (x / last_p - 1.0) >= amp:
                    d_bull.append(t - last_i)
                    cnt_p += 1
                    last_ty, last_i, last_p, changed = "P", t, x, True
            else:
                if ismax and x > last_p:
                    last_i, last_p, changed = t, x, True
                elif ismin and (t - last_i) >= mp and last_p > 0 and \
                        (1.0 - x / last_p) >= amp:
                    d_bear.append(t - last_i)
                    cnt_t += 1
                    last_ty, last_i, last_p, changed = "T", t, x, True
            if changed:
                cmin = min(c[last_i:i + 1])
                cmax = max(c[last_i:i + 1])
        if last_i is not None:
            if cmin is None or c[i] < cmin:
                cmin = c[i]
            if cmax is None or c[i] > cmax:
                cmax = c[i]
            ph_ty[i] = last_ty
            ph_age[i] = i - last_i
            ph_min[i] = cmin
            ph_max[i] = cmax
            # the empirical hazard: where this phase's age sits in the
            # distribution of COMPLETED phases of the same type so far
            src = d_bear if last_ty == "P" else d_bull
            if len(src) >= minph:
                s = sorted(src)
                thr_in[i] = s[min(len(s) - 1, int(p_in * len(s)))]
            src2 = d_bull if last_ty == "P" else d_bear
            if len(src2) >= minph:
                s2 = sorted(src2)
                thr_out[i] = s2[min(len(s2) - 1, int(p_out * len(s2)))]
        n_p[i] = cnt_p
        n_t[i] = cnt_t

    # ---- price confirmation: a real move off the phase extreme ---------
    rise = [False] * n
    fall = [False] * n
    for i in range(n):
        a = atr[i]
        if a is None or a <= 0.0 or ph_min[i] is None:
            continue
        rise[i] = (c[i] - ph_min[i]) >= conf * a
        fall[i] = (ph_max[i] - c[i]) >= conf * a

    sig = [0] * n
    fired = 0
    for i in range(rec, n):
        ty = ph_ty[i]
        th = thr_in[i]
        if ty is None or th is None:
            continue
        if ph_age[i] <= th:
            continue
        if ty == "P" and rise[i] and not rise[i - rec]:
            sig[i] = 1
            fired += 1
        elif ty == "T" and fall[i] and not fall[i - rec]:
            sig[i] = -1
            fired += 1

    ctx.dh_s = ctx.series(sig, "hazard_entry")
    ctx.dh_age = ctx.series(ph_age, "phase_age")
    ctx.dh_out = ctx.series(thr_out, "exit_age")
    ctx.dh_np = ctx.series(n_p, "peaks_dated")
    ctx.dh_nt = ctx.series(n_t, "troughs_dated")
    if d_bull or d_bear:
        b1 = sorted(d_bull)
        b2 = sorted(d_bear)
        ctx.log("%d bull phases (med %s bars), %d bear phases (med %s bars), "
                "%d entries"
                % (len(b1), b1[len(b1) // 2] if b1 else "-",
                   len(b2), b2[len(b2) // 2] if b2 else "-", fired))


def signal(ctx, i):
    s = ctx.dh_s[i]
    return s if s else 0


def exit_signal(ctx, i):
    """Out when the new phase is itself overdue, or a turning point is dated."""
    if not ctx.positions:
        return False
    p = ctx.positions[0]
    e = p["entry_i"]
    if p["side"] == "long":
        if ctx.dh_np[i] > ctx.dh_np[e]:
            return True
    else:
        if ctx.dh_nt[i] > ctx.dh_nt[e]:
            return True
    t = ctx.dh_out[i]
    return t is not None and (i - e) >= t
